messages:
mira: quick brain-dump — I want to propose splitting the policy evaluation stack into two orthogonal pieces: a tiny, hot-path matcher (stateless, indexable) and a slower evaluator kernel for expressive rules. goal: keep p99 down for the 80% simple cases while not losing policy expressiveness for edge-cases.
omar: +1 on the idea. can you sketch what "matcher" inputs/outputs look like?
mira: matcher should accept a minimal request descriptor (tenant, region, model_family, priority_tag, cached_key_flags) and return a ranked shortlist + metadata (compatibility flags, estimated cost bucket). no policy ASTs on the hot path.
leah: how do we keep matcher correctness vs evaluator? soundness vs completeness tradeoff. matcher could be conservative (over-include) to avoid false negatives.
mira: exactly — matcher is allowed to be over-approximate. we then run evaluator (if needed) to prune or enforce strict constraints before final admission. that keeps low-latency hits cheap.
raj: what about caching? if matcher is over-approx then cache misses will hit evaluator more often. TTL/invalidations become critical.
simon: propose two-tier caching: short-lived per-node matcher cache (ms lifetime) + slightly longer cross-node result cache keyed by (tenant, model_version, route_signature) with explicit invalidation on policy change.
nana: infra-bot note: we already have a small cache for route-compat checks in the runtime (node-local). TTL is 500ms today. increasing it might help but increases stale-policy risk.
nana: infra-bot: bumping to 2s reduced evaluator calls in perf tests by ~18% but caused 1 tenant to see delayed rollout by 1s in canary. tradeoff.
leah: we should define cache-key shape precisely. suggested: "tenant|model_hash|region|intent_hash|bucket_window". keep it stable and deterministic.
mira: also need an admission-control hook that can short-circuit based on quota/taints even before evaluator. small ACL checks in matcher.
omar: interface boundaries matter. the matcher must be a deterministic filter fn with no side effects and must be cheap enough to inline in common runtimes (go/c++). evaluator can be a sandboxed service (python/wasm) with richer primitives (time windows, histograms, ML-scored penalties).
raj: what about rollout and backward compatibility? older runtimes expect the current policy DSL. we can implement a translation layer that compiles legacy DSL to matcher+evaluator pairs, and default to evaluator-only for anything that cannot be compiled.
simon: metrics plan: record matcher-hit, matcher-shortlist-size, evaluator-invocations, evaluator-latency, final-decision-reason. add dimension for tenant and route.
leah: testing: we need property tests to assert matcher is a superset of evaluator decisions (i.e., matcher must not drop any candidate that evaluator would accept). nightly job to fuzz policies and compare.
mira: operational: graph of failures we must watch: matcher false negative (application error), evaluator timeout (fallback to safe default model), stale cache causing rollout delay, and admission hook misconfiguration causing rejects.
nana: infra-bot: recommend a progressive rollout: 1) matcher-only shadow mode (no routing changes but collect deltas) 2) matcher + evaluator for canary tenants 3) global rollout with short caches 4) increase cache TTL if stable. include feature-flag gating per-region.
raj: long-term refactor thought: expose a policy "compiler" that emits two artifacts: a compact matcher trie and a serialized evaluator graph. keeps runtime language-agnostic and makes policy packaging a build step.
leah: open question: do we allow tenant-overrides to plug into matcher logic? risk: explosion of cache keys and hot-path churn. maybe tenant-overrides only affect evaluator unless explicitly whitelisted.
mira: agree — default: tenant overrides are evaluator-level. opt-in for matcher-level overrides with quota and validation.
omar: API changes: need a small, backward-compatible payload for routing request that contains precomputed intent_hash and model_family. clients that don't have it fall back to server-side extraction (slower).
simon: also consider a tiny admission scoring step that returns an "estimated_unit_cost" to help the upstream router do cost-based batching. matcher can provide a coarse bucket.
leah: security note: evaluator will run richer expressions, so run it in a least-privileged sandbox (wasm or container). audit logs must capture policy decision id and inputs.
mira: timeline proposal: week 0-2: matcher proto + translation for existing policies; week 3-4: matcher shadow + metrics; week 5: canary evaluator integration; week 6-8: staged rollout. need eng-sre to plan canary tenants and monitoring.
nana: infra-bot: created canary group "policy-kernel-test-1" and scheduled perf job to run matcher shadow across 10k req/s at 2077654350.
raj: two last items: cost of evaluator per-invocation; we may want a budget that automatically downgrades to fallback variants when evaluator budget is exhausted. and clear operator tooling to recompile/preview matcher artifacts.
mira: thanks everyone. I'll draft an RFC with the compiler artifact format, matcher API spec, metrics contract, and the migration checklist. I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
nana: infra-bot: mira pushed draft RFC to docs/rfcs/policy-kernel-split.md (branch mir/policy-kernel).
nana: infra-bot: deploy-bot: perf harness started at 2077654362.
nana: infra-bot: note — if anyone wants shadow logs, tag me and I'll add your handle to the log ACL.
nana: infra-bot: thread closed at 2077654378."
